newsitem.title: IRAN: Quakes hit Iran, casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: Quakes hit Iran, casualties reported.

text.p: Several earthquakes hit northern and western Iran on Friday, one of them causing casualties and damage near the border with Azerbaijan, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

It said an earthquake measuring about six degrees on the Richter scale jolted areas outside Ardabil, a provincial capital 400 km (250 miles) northwest of Tehran, for about 15 seconds and sent residents running from their homes.
"Based on reports available, the quake has caused loss of property and casaulties in certain suburban villages," IRNA said without giving further details.
The earthquake struck at 4.31 p.m. (1301 GMT) and was followed by several aftershocks in the Ardabil area, which is near the Iran-Azerbaijan border, the agency said.
Three minutes earlier and some 350 km (220 miles) away, a quake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit the Kurdish-populated city of Sanandaj, IRNA said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in Sanandaj, which is also a provincial capital, it added.
Iran's northern province of Guilan on the Caspian coast was also shaken by a tremor measuring about four on the Richter scale, but there was no damage, IRNA added.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in northeastern Iran in early February.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in Guilan and neighbouring Zanjan province in 1990.
